messages:
jun: quick heads-up — ran a tiered kv-cache + quantization sweep across US/EU/APAC on H100/A100. seeing a p99 latency spike for long seqlen (>1024) in EU when using q4_0 int8. hitrate looks ok but paging events and eviction churn are high. anyone seen this pattern?

maria: can you drop the raw numbers? which model and batch size?
jun: model=redwood-7b-open, batch=8 (client small bursts), seqlen dist = mix(16:50%,128:30%,1024+:20%). throughput H100(us)=~27k tok/s for seqlen512 baseline (fp16), A100(us)=~17.5k. with q4_0 on EU-H100 p50~12ms p95~58ms p99~210ms (p99 baseline fp16 ~130ms).
samir: kernel selection? did the runtime fallback to generic matmul for any ops with q4_0? that often kills p99 on some driver combos.
jun: good call — noticed a kernel-fallback warning in the serve log: "kernel no-match -> using cpu-generic" for fused-attn on a few shards. suspect quantized weight layout differs and our kernel matcher didn't pick optimized path.
maria: linked dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/kv/2076543210 — region tabs show EU owning 60% of p99 regressions. also EU H100 fleet has an older CUDA/driver patch (470.x) on a subset.
elaine: on the eval front, there is a small quality delta: q4_0 produced a 0.8% drop in generation F1 on our 5k regression set (mainly for long-form summarization). probably tied to int8 rounding + paging-induced token drops on late timesteps.
samir: eviction policy? LRU or adaptive? aggressive evict during high churn can boost throughput but hurts hitrate for long-running contexts.
jun: running tiered config: hot-tier (KV in GPU), warm-tier (host pinned), cold (nvme). eviction=adaptive with watermark_hi=0.78 watermark_lo=0.58, prefetch_window=8. reducing prefetch_window -> lowers host transfers but increases misses. observed: prefetch=8 => hitrate 86% overall, p99 EU down to 160ms; prefetch=4 => hitrate 81%, p99 up to 240ms but lower avg GPU memory pressure.
maria: posting a concise repro command:
```
./bench_kvcache --model redwood-7b-open --quant q4_0 --gpu h100 --region eu --batch 8 --seqlen-mix 16:50,128:30,1024:20 --prefetch 8 --evict adaptive
```
jun: log excerpt (evict churn):
```
[2026-02-12T08:21:43Z] pager: evict shard=3 count=512 reason=watermark_hi
[2026-02-12T08:21:43Z] pager: prefetch miss shard=14 -> host-read 4MB
[2026-02-12T08:21:45Z] serve: kernel-fallback fused-attn shard=7 reason=layout-mismatch
```
maria: confirmed driver mismatch on eu-h100-legacy pool, scheduling driver upgrade to 525.x tomorrow. that should fix kernel fallback if it's the only issue.
elaine: for the q4_0 quality regression we should run a short ablation: q4_0 vs q4_1 vs fp16 on the 10k long-form eval set and break down errors by prefix length. also include decode temp deterministic seeds.
samir: also consider recompiling kernels with updated weight-layout detection for q4_*; sometimes a pattern fix removes the generic fallback. small patch gave us ~40% p99 improvement last quarter.
ci-bot: perf-run uploaded: https://ci.internal/runs/2076543210 (artifacts: logs, flamegraphs, kv-hitrate.csv)
jun: next steps: 1) driver patch on EU fleet, 2) recompile kernels with q4 detection, 3) ablation q4_0/q4_1/fp16 on 10k eval, 4) try prefetch_window sweep [4,8,12] on a single shard to find sweet spot.
maria: sounds good — i'll queue driver rollout and kick off the ablation after. tagging infra for canary first. :thumbsup:
elaine: ack — i'll prepare the eval slice and add jittered prompts to stress long tails.
samir: i'll prototype the detection patch and run local flamegraphs.
ci-bot: scheduled job 2076543245 -> status: queued
jun: thanks team — keeping this thread for follow-ups."
